items.en: Some of your ships suffer from low combat readiness and could experience malfunctions during battle.\n\nTheir combat systems can be powered down to avoid malfunctions and allow the ships to make their best speed to escape.

Forces a battle in which the disengaging forces attempt to get away.

Reduces the combat readiness of all disengaging ships as if they were deployed into combat.\n\nAlso slows down your fleet for a while as your forces require time to reorganize after the harassing action.
Unable to harass the retreating forces either due to standing down or not having any combat-ready ships.
Lets the other fleet leave in peace.\n\nYour fleet does not need to reorganize after the encounter and is not slowed down.
Attack the opposing fleet.\n\nIf you inflict enough damage before retreating, you will be able to disengage without being pursued.

Ends the battle with no risk of being harried by the opposing fleet.

As the enemy remains in control of the battlespace, you won't be able to conduct any salvage operations.

If your fleet hasn't taken any hostile actions, disengaging will not do any damage to your standing with the opposing faction.

Ends the battle without any risk of pursuit. The opposing fleet may still harry your retreat.

As the enemy remains in control of the battlespace, you won't be able to conduct any salvage operations.

If your fleet hasn't taken any hostile actions, disengaging will not do any damage to your standing with the opposing faction.

Attempt to retreat from battle. The opposing fleet may pursue and force a battle, or may let you go.

As the enemy remains in control of the battlespace, you won't be able to conduct any salvage operations.

If your fleet hasn't taken any hostile actions, disengaging - without damaging any pursuing ships - will do the least damage to your standing with the opposing faction.
Organize a boarding action. Requires marines and likely to result in serious personnel losses.
Attack the ship before it has a chance to complete repairs.\n\nThere is a chance that the ship will be destroyed entirely.
Let the enemy ship finish emergency repairs and withdraw.

Ships assigned to the boarding task force approach the enemy ship and dock with it.

Offers the best combat odds to the assault teams and a high chance of success.

If the ship being boarded self-destructs, the ships involved in the boarding action will take heavy damage and may be destroyed.

The boarding task force maintains a safe distance and launches assault teams equipped with personal propulsion systems.\n\nGives the defenders a significant combat advantage and a higher chance to get away, but does not risk the ships in the boarding task force.
Recall the task force and cancel the boarding action, allowing the enemy ship to withdraw.

Welcome to the Starsector campaign!

Since you're playing in iron mode, you'll only be able to save the game when you exit, and won't be able to load another game without exiting (and saving) your current game first.

Try to avoid taking on fleets much bigger than yours, or ones that have bigger ships, and please remember that it's a work-in-progress so bugs will occasionally happen.

Good luck!

Some of the ships marked for deployment are at dangerously low combat readiness (below 20%).

Bringing the systems on these ships to combat power levels is likely to cause critical malfunctions - dealing damage, disabling some weapons and engines for the duration of the battle, and causing further critical malfunctions during the deployment.

Running these risks - which include the outright destruction of a ship - is usually a measure of last resort.
Proceed with the deployment
Reconsider

Some of the ships marked for deployment are at low combat readiness (below 40%).\n\nTheir weapon systems and engines are likely to suffer malfunctions and become temporarily disabled during sustained use.

You can select which ships to deploy at the beginning of each battle, and deploy reinforcements as the battle goes on.

Deploying a ship reduces its combat readiness by a fixed amount. In addition, ships will begin to gradually lose combat readiness after their peak readiness time runs out.

Recovering combat readiness takes time and consumes valuable supplies.

You've made changes to the ship's loadout, but have not adjusted the weapon groups.\n\nWeapons will be automatically assigned to groups when you deploy the ship for combat, but it's a good idea to make the assignments manually.
Adjust weapon groups
Never mind

In the cargo/trade screen, you can:

- Left-click to pick up a stack
- Shift-click to pick up items from a stack one at a time
- Shift-click and hold, then drag to pick up a specific quantity
- Control-click to transfer an entire stack without picking it up

Your fleet has been hit by a hyperspace storm! One of your ships has taken damage and its combat readiness has been reduced.\n\nStorm strikes can also knock your fleet off course, but an \"Emergency Burn\" lets your fleet to get back on course more easily and allows it to punch through storms.

Congratulations, you just bought a new ship!

It doesn't have any weapons or hullmods installed, so it's a good idea to get it outfitted.

You'll also need to make sure you have enough personnel to crew it.
Open the refit screen

Congratulations, you just bought a new fighter wing!

Fighter wing combat readiness represents the number of replacement fighter chassis available, but these can only be used if you have a ship with a flight deck in your fleet.

New fighters will take off from a nearby flight deck to replace any losses taken in combat. As long as your fleet has a ship with proper repair facilities (i.e. a flight deck), a fighter wing can not be completely lost, even if its combat readiness is reduced to zero.

When refitting a ship while docked at a space station, you can mount both the weapons in your cargo hold and the ones available for purchase at the station.\n\nUndoing the changes to the ship's loadout (or simply unmounting the purchased weapons) will refund the credits used, but only if you haven't navigated away from the refit screen.

Warning: you're taking more salvage than your fleet has the capacity to carry.

This will result in greatly increased daily supply consumption and a reduced travel speed.

It's recommended that you either take less salvage or head for a nearby station to sell off the excess.

Your fleet is carrying more cargo than it has capacity for.

This will result in greatly increased daily supply consumption and a reduced travel speed.

It's recommended that you either jettison some of the cargo now or head to a station quickly so you can sell off the excess. You can jettison cargo from the crew/cargo screen.
Open the crew/cargo screen

Your fleet is carrying more fuel than it has capacity for.

This will result in greatly increased daily supply consumption and a reduced travel speed.

It's recommended that you either jettison some of the fuel now or head to a station quickly so you can sell off the excess. You can jettison fuel from the crew/cargo screen.

Your fleet is carrying more personnel than it has capacity for.

This will result in greatly increased daily supply consumption and a reduced travel speed.

It's recommended that you head to a nearby market so you can drop them off there.
Your fleet is running low on fuel.\n\nIf it runs out of fuel in hyperspace, it will drift towards the nearest star system and may become stranded if you're not able to acquire more fuel there.

Your fleet is running low on supplies.

If it runs out of supplies, all repairs will stop and ships will start to lose combat readiness over time. After more than a couple of days without supplies, the fleet begins to run the risk of accidents that range from minor (such as the loss of some cargo) to critical (losing a ship).

It's recommended that you acquire more supplies as quickly as possible.

To reduce supply consumption, you can suspend any ongoing ship repairs. A last resort way to get more supplies is to scuttle one of your ships.

The commands to do so are available on the fleet screen.
